 Key points
 The Finance Ministry's Department of Expenditure revised DA for employees on 5th CPC pay scales to 497% of basic pay from 1 July 2026. 
 The rate rises from 483% of basic pay, a 14 percentage point increase. 
 It covers only employees still drawing pay under the 5th Pay Commission — not the much larger group on 7th CPC pay, who get a separate DA rate. 
 The memorandum is signed by Under Secretary Manoj Kumar Jain, and may also be brought to the notice of all concerned. 
 Advertisement
 Employees still drawing pay on 5th Central Pay Commission scales get Dearness Allowance of 497% of basic pay from 1 July 2026, up from 483%, the Department of Expenditure has ordered.
 The office memorandum of the Finance Ministry’s Department of Expenditure is signed by Manoj Kumar Jain, Under Secretary to the Government of India.
 The revision applies only to employees who are still paid on the pre-revised 5th Pay Commission scales — a small group, mainly in autonomous bodies and legacy posts, since most central government staff moved to later pay commissions long ago.
 The far larger group of central government employees, those on 7th CPC pay, is not covered by this order. They draw DA at 63% of basic pay from July 2026 , a separate rate set under the 7th Pay Commission’s own formula. State government employees follow their own state’s DA orders.
 Old and new DA rates
 Period DA rate (5th CPC scale) 
 Before 1 July 2026 483% of Basic Pay 
 From 1 July 2026 497% of Basic Pay 
 What the higher rate means in rupees
 On our calculation, on basic pay of ₹10,000 a month the old DA of 483% worked out to ₹48,300 a month. At the new rate of 497% it is ₹49,700 a month — ₹1,400 a month more on every ₹10,000 of basic pay. The order itself sets only the percentage.
 The new rate is 14 percentage points above the earlier one. Dearness Allowance is revised twice a year, from 1 January and 1 July, to offset inflation.
 Why some employees are still on 5th CPC scales
 A few central government employees and autonomous-body staff were never moved to later pay scales, so their basic pay is still the figure fixed under the 5th Pay Commission. Because that basic pay is much smaller than under later pay commissions, the DA percentage on it runs far higher to make up the difference.
 The memorandum may also be brought to the notice of all concerned. A Hindi version of the order is attached to it.
 Source: Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure, Office Memorandum No. 1/2(iii)/2026-E.II(B) — revision of DA for employees on 5th Central Pay Commission scales w.e.f. 1 July 2026.

 Critical AdSense behaviour: adsbygoogle.push({}) does NOT bind to
 a specific . It says "process the next unbound in DOM
 order." So if you push N times, AdSense binds the first N 
 slots it finds.
 Live investigation (2026-05-29) showed the right sidebar still
 loading late on indianpaycalculator.in. DOM order of :
 1. LEFT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-left)
 2-5. Display banners (4× AdBanner inside page content)
 6. RIGHT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-right, after main slot)
 7. Mobile anchor (StickyAnchorAd at body end)
 Previously this script pushed twice (one per sidebar). Those 2
 pushes bound LEFT + Display#1, NOT LEFT + RIGHT. The other 5
 slots only got bound as AdBanner.client:visible islands hydrated
 on scroll — meaning the right sidebar was bound 6th, after the
 user scrolled past every in-page banner. That's the "right side
 opens very late" complaint.
